name: xbert-config-audit
description: Is XBert configured consistently across your book? Spot inconsistencies, gaps, and drift in one pass.

x-xbert.tagline: Is XBert configured consistently across your book? Spot inconsistencies, gaps, and drift in one pass.
prerequisites: XBert account with multiple client tenants in a Connect
Workflow and XBert configurations active on at least some clients
Practice owner or manager-level access to the Connect
x-xbert.longDescription:
Your XBert rule set should look the same across clients in the same segment. In practice it almost never does — different staff onboarded different clients, defaults drifted as the rule library grew, and 'always-on' rules ended up on most clients but not all. Config Audit is the quarterly pass that surfaces that drift before it costs you.

The plugin reads the per-client XBert configuration across your Connect, fingerprints each rule's enablement pattern, and reports three things: rules enabled inconsistently within a segment, rules that should be on everywhere but are missing on N clients, and rules that have been switched off (drift). Then it pairs each finding with a bulk-normalisation move so the cleanup is concrete, not abstract. This is distinct from XBert Workflow Review — that plugin looks at templates and schedules; this one looks at XBert rule configuration itself.

useCases.title: Quarterly config sweep
useCases.description: Once a quarter, run the audit to catch drift before it becomes systemic — clients onboarded last quarter often miss rules added recently.

useCases.title: Post-onboarding consistency check
useCases.description: After a batch of new clients comes on, confirm they all have the rule set the practice considers baseline.

useCases.title: Pre-audit / pre-review preparation
useCases.description: Before an internal QA pass or external review, make sure the practice can demonstrate consistent XBert configuration across the book.

useCases.title: Standardisation campaign
useCases.description: When the practice decides to standardise on a new ruleset, use the audit to drive the rollout — see who needs what enabled and what disabled.

benefits.title: Inconsistency, gap and drift in one pass
benefits.description: Three distinct fingerprints — inconsistencies inside a segment, gaps where always-on rules are missing, and drift where rules have been switched off.

benefits.title: Bulk-normalisation moves named
benefits.description: Every finding is paired with the specific bulk update that resolves it, so cleanup is a list of decisions, not a research project.

benefits.title: Quarterly-ready Word output
benefits.description: Word document with executive summary, segment-by-segment breakdown and the normalisation backlog — ready to action with the team.

workflow: Confirm the Connect tenant and the client segmentation rule (default = by industry tag, fallback = whole book)
Plugin pulls the Connect account review, configuration assignments and rule list via XBert MCP
Per-segment fingerprints are computed, inconsistencies / gaps / drift are classified
Word document is produced with the audit findings and a named bulk-normalisation backlog
